sections.heading: C — Traffic Laws and Regulations
sections.markdown:
## C — Traffic Laws and Regulations

FACT_ID: sec06-F01 | anchor: A01
You must obey every traffic law while driving on a street or highway, obey all lawful orders and directions of a police officer, and operate your vehicle as traffic signs, signals and pavement markings indicate [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec06-F02 | anchor: A01
Drive on the right half of the roadway, pass oncoming vehicles on the right, give opposite-direction traffic at least half of the main traveled roadway on narrow roads, and when moving slower than other traffic you should use the extreme right lane [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec06-F03 | anchor: A01
You may use the left half of the roadway when overtaking a vehicle going your way on a road with two or three lanes of moving traffic and no oncoming traffic, when an obstruction blocks your side and oncoming vehicles are not using the left half, or when driving on a one-way street [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec06-F04 | anchor: A01
The left half of the roadway is forbidden on a road with four or more lanes of moving traffic unless signs say otherwise, near the top of a hill or on a curve, within one hundred feet of or inside an intersection or railroad crossing, and within one hundred feet of a bridge or tunnel when oncoming vehicles cannot be seen [A01].
Why it matters: the one-hundred-foot distances at intersections, crossings, bridges and tunnels are the testable numbers.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec06-F05 | anchor: A01
Passing on the right is permitted when the vehicle ahead is about to turn left without driving off the pavement or main traveled roadway, on a paved road with two or more marked lanes in each direction, or on a one-way street with two or more marked lanes [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec06-F06 | anchor: A01
On a one-way roadway you must drive only in the direction the posted signs indicate [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec06-F07 | anchor: A01
On a road marked with traffic lanes you must drive entirely within one lane, change lanes only after checking that the change is safe, and use the lane the signs or pavement markings assign [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec06-F08 | anchor: A02
Your following distance must stay reasonable and prudent for the speed, the traffic, the road and the weather, and a vehicle that is towing another must leave enough room ahead for an overtaking vehicle to move into safely [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec06-F09 | anchor: A02
On a highway divided by a barrier or an unpaved space you must not cross or drive through the divider except at an opening or paved crossover that signs do not prohibit [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec06-F10 | anchor: A02
You must signal every time you slow down, turn or change lanes, even when no other vehicle is in sight, and signals must be given for at least one hundred feet, about five car lengths, before the maneuver, with a longer signal advisable at higher speeds [A02].
Why it matters: one hundred feet equals about five car lengths, and the signal is required even on an empty road.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec06-F11 | anchor: A02
Hand signals must be used when the vehicle's turn signals are not working, and signaling never gives you the right to make the move until you have checked that it can be completed without interfering with other traffic [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec06-F12 | anchor: A02
Keep your foot off the brake pedal whenever you are not actually braking, because a lit stop lamp sends following drivers a false stop signal [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec06-F13 | anchor: A02
You must stop at least fifteen feet from the nearest rail of a railroad crossing when an electric or mechanical signal warns of a train, when a gate is lowered or a flagman signals, when a train within one thousand five hundred feet sounds an audible warning, or when an approaching train is visible and close enough to be a hazard [A02].
Why it matters: fifteen feet from the rail and one thousand five hundred feet of train warning are two separate numbers.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec06-F14 | anchor: A03
Excessive speed for conditions is the major cause of most crashes, and the basic speed law forbids driving faster than is reasonable and prudent for the area, the road and traffic, pedestrians, weather and light [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec06-F15 | anchor: A03
You must not exceed the posted maximum speed limit, must not drive below a posted minimum speed limit, and must not drive so slowly that you hold back other traffic, pulling off the road or changing route if you cannot keep up [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec06-F16 | anchor: A03
If you drive more slowly than traffic on a multilane road, stay in the right-hand lane so others can pass on your left, and never take part in any race, speed contest or speed exhibition on a public street or highway [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec06-F17 | anchor: A03
Lower speed limits apply near schools and playgrounds, at school crossing signs while children are present, and on residential and business streets [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec06-F18 | anchor: A03
Parking is prohibited anywhere your vehicle is hazardous to other traffic, where it will be towed, on a sidewalk, in front of or so close to a driveway that it interferes with its use, and within or so close to an intersection that it interferes with traffic [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec06-F19 | anchor: A03
Parking is also prohibited in front of or so close to a fire hydrant that it could interfere with the hydrant's use, on or so close to a crosswalk that it blocks drivers' view of pedestrians, where official signs or markings prohibit standing or parking, and on a bridge, elevated structure or inside a tunnel [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0028]

sections.heading: C — Traffic Laws and Regulations (continued)
sections.markdown:
## C — Traffic Laws and Regulations (continued)

FACT_ID: sec06-F20 | anchor: A03
Double parking, stopping on the roadway side of another car at the edge of the road, is prohibited whether or not you stay in the vehicle, and so is parking more than twelve inches from the curb [A03].
Why it matters: twelve inches from the curb is the measurable parking rule.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec06-F21 | anchor: A03
You may not park in a passenger or freight loading zone, anywhere that leaves less than ten feet of street width for free movement of traffic, or on a public road to repair a vehicle except in an emergency, wash it, or display it for sale [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec06-F22 | anchor: A04
A vehicle may not be parked so that it sticks out of a marked space unless it is larger than the space, and no vehicle may stay parked on a public street or highway continuously for more than twenty-four hours [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec06-F23 | anchor: A04
A space marked with the international symbol of accessibility may be used only when you display the placard or plate issued to the disabled person being transported, and the access aisle beside such a space must stay clear for wheelchair lifts, ramps and other mobility devices [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec06-F24 | anchor: A04
In a tow-away zone you must not park or stop even momentarily during the hours on the official sign, except when blocked by traffic, and a vehicle left there is towed by the police, whom you contact for recovery information [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec06-F25 | anchor: A04
Driving with more than three persons in the front seat may constitute interference with the driver, which is prohibited [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec06-F26 | anchor: A04
Before leaving a vehicle unattended, shut off the engine, lock the ignition and take the key, set the parking brake, and turn the wheels toward the curb if the vehicle is on a grade [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec06-F27 | anchor: A04
When you hear an emergency vehicle's siren, bell or horn or see its flashing red or blue lamps you must give it a clear path and stop, without panicking or jamming on the brakes, by reducing speed, locating the vehicle and its direction, and moving out of its path [A04].
Why it matters: the manual stresses a calm pull-over, not a panic stop.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec06-F28 | anchor: A04
When an emergency vehicle is right behind you in heavy traffic, continue slowly until you can clear its way, and when you come upon a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, slow or stop as the situation demands and, if it is safe, keep an empty lane between your vehicle and it [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec06-F29 | anchor: A04
Funeral processions and convoys have the right of way at intersections, their vehicles usually use headlamps for identification while the first and last vehicles usually carry distinctive markings, and you should not drive between vehicles in a funeral procession [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec06-F30 | anchor: A05
A highly reflective eighteen-inch triangular slow-moving vehicle emblem must be displayed on the rear of vehicles designed to travel at twenty-five miles per hour or less, and when you see it you should reduce speed and approach cautiously [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec06-F31 | anchor: A05
You must not pass on the right shoulder of the highway, and you must not pass when approaching a hill or curve without seven hundred to one thousand feet of clear distance ahead [A05].
Why it matters: the clear-distance range for hills and curves is a classic numeric item.
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec06-F32 | anchor: A05
You must not pass when the maneuver cannot be completed without interfering with the safety of an oncoming vehicle and before a yellow line appears in your lane, and when you are being passed it is unlawful to increase your speed [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec06-F33 | anchor: A06
You must not pass when a solid yellow line is in your lane, which is announced by a yellow no passing zone pennant on the left side of the road ahead, nor when a school bus on the same roadway has its flashing lights operating [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec06-F34 | anchor: A06
You must not pass within one hundred feet of or while crossing any intersection or railroad crossing, nor within one hundred feet of a posted narrow bridge, viaduct or tunnel, and the end of a no passing zone only means visibility has improved, not that passing is safe [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec06-F35 | anchor: A07
When vehicles reach an intersection at the same time you yield to the car on the right, and when turning left you yield to all oncoming traffic close enough to be a hazard [A07].
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec06-F36 | anchor: A07
You yield to all traffic on the protected route, stopping first where a stop is required, and you must stop and yield when entering any public street or road from an alley, driveway or farmyard [A07].
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec06-F37 | anchor: A07
When a light turns green you yield to pedestrians and to vehicles still caught in the intersection before you proceed [A07].
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0032]

Misconceptions: signaling is required even when no one is around and does not by itself give you the right to move; the end of a no passing zone means better visibility, not permission to pass; a left turn yields to oncoming traffic even on a green light; speeding up while being passed is unlawful; the railroad stop is at least fifteen feet from the rail, not from the crossing sign; the slow-moving vehicle emblem marks vehicles built for twenty-five miles per hour or less, not any slow driver.

Mnemonics: One hundred feet of signal, one hundred feet of no-left-half and no-passing at intersections, crossings, bridges and tunnels; fifteen feet back from the rail; twelve inches to the curb, ten feet of street left free, twenty-four hours is the parking limit; three in the front seat is the most.

Glossary: basic speed law (never faster than reasonable and prudent for conditions); protected route (the road whose traffic has the right of way at an intersection); double parking (stopping on the roadway side of a car parked at the curb); tow-away zone (a signed area where even a momentary stop brings a tow); slow-moving vehicle emblem (the reflective orange triangle on vehicles built for twenty-five miles per hour or less); access aisle (the striped space beside an accessible parking stall).

Dynamic facts: the statute references printed beside the emergency vehicle and parking rules can be renumbered between printings and are not stated as stable knowledge; the distances, times and right-of-way rules are stable rules of this printing.

ranked.label: Keeping right, passing right, lanes and following

items.why: the chapter teaches both topics through diagrams of intersections and passing situations, so a learner must decide who yields or whether a pass is legal from a described scene, not just recall a number
the one-hundred-foot, fifteen-foot, twelve-inch and ten-foot rules are discrete values that cards and quiz items cover

corpus_stability.reason: The Hawaii Driver's Manual is a periodically reprinted reference (imprint HMG 5/2023, copyright line through 2023); the obeying officers and signs, driving on the right and when the left half may be used, passing on the right, lane use, following distance, divided highways, required signals, railroad crossings, speed rules, prohibited parking, tow-away zones, unattended vehicles, emergency vehicles, funeral processions, the slow-moving vehicle emblem, no-passing situations and right-of-way rules rules on pages 26–32 are statutory and procedural content that changes less than once a year, so no BlockedProbe.
